ops.title: daemonkit v1: four architecture decisions taken 2026-07-28 (lifecycle axes, archive-aside, spawnedsession, StableProgram)
ops.body:
User decisions on four of the Phase-0 census's eleven open questions (census §4, at `~/.claude/projects/-Users-yasyf-Code-daemonkit/phase0/contracts/census.md`). **Settled — do not re-litigate.** The remaining seven are being settled by measurement.

## Q9 — `daemon.State` and `daemon.LifecycleState` stay TWO SEPARATE AXES

The plan's *"ONE lifecycle enum owned by `daemon`: starting → ready → draining → closed"* was literally neither existing enum, and collapsing them would have been a **wire-visible break in two consumers' own frozen protocols** — not a rename.

- `daemon.LifecycleState` (`daemon/lifecycle.go:14-25`) is the **publication phase**: `runtime_starting` / `runtime_ready` / `runtime_failed` / `runtime_draining`. It has no `closed`.
- `daemon.State` (`daemon/peer.go:10-19`) is **health**: `healthy` / `degraded` / `failed`. It is serialized on the wire — cc-interact puts it on JSON as `"state"` (`daemon/protocol.go:40`) and branches on all three (`launcher.go:230,235,238,284`); synckit ships `string(value.State)` (`internal/runtimehealth/observation.go:24`) and asserts on it (`daemon/serve_test.go:61`); reposync and cookiesync read that JSON.

**Decision:** the health axis survives as its own wire-visible value. "One enum" applies **only to the publication phase**, which gains `closed`. The two axes are genuinely orthogonal — a daemon can be `ready` and `degraded` simultaneously — and the plan's one-enum line becomes one-enum-per-axis. No consumer break, and no compatibility shim.

## Q11 — durable state ARCHIVES ASIDE UNIFORMLY, including the controller state store

`service/controller.go:55-60` deliberately withholds this policy today. The counter-evidence weighed and rejected: a store the new release cannot read bricks `synckitd install` and `synckitd uninstall` — the only paths that converge the LaunchAgents, reached through exactly one function (`daemon/install.go:28`) with no second path.

**Decision:** archive aside with a logged path, uniformly. Contract C1's *"never a fatal open"* holds everywhere with no exception. This kills the `002e2e9a` wedge class outright — a fixed release can always supersede its own failed-era state, including through the **fourth door** the census found (`NewController` aborting on `verify` failure, which includes `launchctl print` returning any unclassified code, `controller.go:415`).

**The obligation this creates:** desired state must genuinely be the caller's fresh set on every `Converge`, so an empty store costs exactly one `Converge` to rebuild. That must be **proven**, not assumed — it is the premise the decision rests on. The residual risk is agents installed by old versions, which carry no ownership marker (open Q5); until that is solved, an archived store can orphan them.

## Q8 — `spawnedsession` is RESHAPED into `proc.Run` with a session option

Ten exported symbols across `proc/` and `wire/` (`SpawnedSessionEndpoint`, `SpawnedSessionIdentity`, `PreparedChild.ClaimSpawnedSession`, `SpawnConfig.SpawnedSession`, `SpawnConfig.ExpectedSignature`, `NewSignatureDigest`, `wire.NewSpawnedClient`, `wire.SpawnedClientConfig`, `wire.RunSpawnedSession`, `wire.SpawnedSessionConfig`) together **are** synckit's `"spawned"` manifest service kind — all of `synckit/rpc/spawned.go` (82 lines) plus `internal/synctransport/transport.go:105-133`, dispatched from the manifest at `daemon/transport.go:36`.

**Decision:** reshape into one verb with a session option. This preserves the unique property — **K16, ownership of a file descriptor proven before it is closed, which is not derivable from `proc.Record`** — while collapsing ten exported symbols into one.

**Requires a synckit PR in the same release train** to move `rpc/spawned.go` onto the new shape. Note that reposync is `"resident"` today but the manifest is declarative consumer config, so any consumer can select `"spawned"` tomorrow: **a zero-caller sweep would get this wrong**, which is contamination class (iii) from the census safety rule.

## Q4 — `service.StableProgram` FOLDS INTO a `service.Install` verb that stages automatically

`StableProgram`/`StableProgramFrom` have zero references anywhere including their own tests (which call the unexported implementation) — yet they are the shipped remedy for open P1 `74be91d`, and the field state is confirmed: three labels on the remote box point at deleted versioned paths.

**Decision:** rather than keeping the export and driving adoption, staging becomes **automatic and invisible** — consumers call `Install`, never `Stage`, so there is no adoption gap to drive and no bypass to police (`74be91d` names synckit's `canonicalHelperProgram` as the current bypass). This is new API design in Phase 2 rather than adoption of an already-shipped primitive.

Two consequences: the **build-keyed vs digest-keyed** split (`stableprogram.go:49` vs `:68`, two policies under one name held apart by a cross-policy refusal guard) collapses to **digest-keyed only** — digest keying is what makes persisted Caskroom paths unrepresentable, which is the actual fix for `74be91d`. And `Install` becomes the natural owner of the **plist ownership marker** (open Q5), since it is the verb that emits the plist.
